answer: An aspiring-page record carries `name` (the unresolved page name), `page` (the source page containing the link), `pos` (the start of the unresolved link), and `ref` (the reference identifying that occurrence). X-Ray does not underline it, because `aspiring-page` is a `range`-less object type that the lens doesn't show.

Memory for: Which attributes does an aspiring-page record carry, and will the X-Ray lens underline it in the editor?
[1] X-Ray.md (Activation)
  Limitations: * `range`-less objects (`page`, `tag`, `aspiring-page`, `anchor`) aren’t shown — except a tag that occurs only inside a comment, which the indexer gives a range, so X-Ray underlines it (and its card won’t show `inComment`, since `xrayInfo` calls the indexers directly, skipping the comment-marking pass). / * Constructs that the editor renders as a widget may not always show the underline. Hover still works, the tooltip will appear.
  X-Ray is an editor lens that shows you the structure SilverBullet’s indexer sees in your document. When switched on, every text range the indexer extracts as an [[Object]] is underlined. When you hover your mouse over it, it will show you all the attributes extracted as [[YAML]]. / You may also be interested in the [[Graph View]].
[2] Tag/aspiring-page.md (aspiring-page)
  Attributes: * `name`: unresolved page name. / * `page`: source page containing the link. / * `pos`: start of the unresolved link. / * `ref`: reference identifying that occurrence. / Records are rebuilt when the source page is indexed. Creating the target page removes its aspiring-page entries.
[3] CHANGELOG.md (CHANGELOG)
  2.8.0: * [[X-Ray]]: an editor lens (run `Editor: Toggle X-Ray`) to inspect indexed objects inline. / * New built-in [[Guide/Journal|Journal]] library. / * Runtime API: Expose objects (with filter) `/.runtime/objects/*` for external integrations and the [[CLI]], see [[Runtime API]]. / * New `SB_DISABLE_SERVICE_WORKER` : server-side switch to disable the client service worker for all clients, this will disable sync (all loads and saves will go directly to the server) and disable any offline support. / * UX: now showing spinners instead of underlying (Lua) code in states where widgets aren’t ready to render yet (e.g. before an initial index hasn’t completed) / * Fix: indexed `range` for `data` blocks (and `#tag` data blocks) now points at the YAML content instead of the surrounding fence markers. Multi-document blocks now compute per-doc ranges correctly.
[4] Tag/ambiguous-link.md (ambiguous-link)
  Like [[Tag/aspiring-page|aspiring pages]], these records are produced by the relation indexer and are recomputed whenever the page is re-indexed, so an ambiguity disappears from the index as soon as it is fixed (by qualifying the link, or by renaming one of the colliding pages).
[5] Guide/Add Structure and Query.md (Tag it)
  Under the hood: These page attributes are called [[Frontmatter|frontmatter]]. To inspect their source, choose **Edit source** from the form’s ⋯ menu (or **Alt-click** on the form). The form stores a block like this at the very beginning of `Photo Walk`: / ```markdown / --- / tags: outing / status: planned / date: "2026-06-14" / --- / ``` / The two `---` lines mark the block’s boundaries. Inside, [[YAML]] writes each attribute as `name: value`. Your original notes follow the closing `---`. Move the cursor out o ...
Exact facts:
- [1] Run ${widgets.commandButton "Editor: Toggle X-Ray"}. The setting is sticky, it persists across page navigations and reloads until you run the command again.
- [3] Fix: YAML data blocks split only on standalone `---` lines. X-Ray includes attributes added during indexing.
